College Project Overview

About Chemical Awareness

Empowering consumers and university students with transparent chemical literacy and evidence-based formulation analysis.

Academic Project Mission

The Chemical Awareness project originated as a college research initiative aimed at demystifying the complex chemical formulations found on consumer labels. While modern packaging lists IUPAC and INCI names (such as Sodium Lauryl Sulfate, Phenoxyethanol, and Linear Alkylbenzene Sulfonate), consumers often lack the toxicological context needed to understand functional purposes, dermal tolerance thresholds, and environmental persistence.

Our primary goal is to provide a clean, accessible, and scientifically grounded reference platform that bridges the gap between public regulatory data and everyday purchasing choices.

Core Guiding Principles

  • Zero Invented Information: All ingredients, functional roles, CAS identifiers, and safety notes are strictly sourced from verified regulatory dossiers and primary product labeling.
  • Scientific Objectivity: Evaluations distinguish clearly between transient mechanical irritation (e.g. concentrated surfactants) and systemic hazards (e.g. endocrine disruption).
  • Data Transparency: All methodology rubrics, survey datasets, and product records are open and inspectable.
  • Accessibility & Speed: Built using lightweight, standard web technologies without heavy frameworks to ensure optimal performance on all devices.

Technical Architecture & Stack

This project is engineered as a clean, modular, client-side web application adhering to modern web standards:

  • Build Tool: Vite for lightning-fast module bundling and development
  • Logic Layer: Pure JavaScript ES Modules (ESM) with zero third-party framework overhead
  • Markup & Styling: Semantic HTML5 and pure CSS3 with custom variables and responsive design
  • Data Storage: Lightweight, structured JSON data architecture with continuous schema validation

Educational Project Notice

This website is an academic demonstration developed for educational purposes to raise awareness of consumer chemical formulations and toxicological standards. The information provided here does not constitute medical, dermatological, or diagnostic advice.
